title: Odile and the Oath
premise: Vesper Ishikawa, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead in the ivory she carves, has survived three years in Greyhallow by selling charms small enough to escape the Wardens' notice. When a scholar shows her a century-old book of prophecies and tonight's date is written on its final page beside her own name, she is seized by the Crown's inquisitors — for the prophecy names her as either the unmaker of the Hollow King or his bride. The king, Aldric, is slowly being devoured by an oath-sworn entity wearing his crown, a bargain struck to hold back the long winter. As Vesper and Aldric fall in love against every law and loyalty between them, she discovers the prophecy can be rewritten only by someone who gives up what the dead gave her: her hearing. In the end, Vesper carves the binding into the king's own crown-bone at the cost of her gift and nearly her life, unbinding Aldric from the entity as winter breaks; they rule nothing together, but they are free.
about_author: Emrys Coldharbour is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring medieval bone reliquaries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about craftspeople, oaths, and the quiet violence of institutions, and live somewhere cold enough to respect the weather.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finishes a luck-charm for a nervous bride while the dead murmur complaints through the whalebone, then meets a charming scholar named Ilsa at a night market. Ilsa shows her a prophecy book whose last page bears tomorrow's date — and Vesper's name. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Greyhallow After Curfew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She burns her ledgers and plans to flee, but the Wardens arrive first, tipped off by someone who knew her mother's craft. Arrested alongside Ilsa, she hears a dead Warden's bones warn: 'They want you alive.' Beat: betrayal and the collapse of her careful ordinary life.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Inquisitor Serane Hale interrogates her with unsettling gentleness, revealing the Crown has hunted a 'bone-speaker' for a generation. Vesper learns the prophecy names two outcomes: the Hollow King unmade, or wed. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance as she refuses both futures aloud.

chapters.title: What the Crown Carries
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The king wakes inside his own body like a tenant, watching the thing in the crown sign decrees with his hands. He has learned to leave messages in frost. Tonight the frost spells a name he doesn't know: Ishikawa. Beat: isolation cracking into desperate hope.

chapters.title: An Audience of One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Brought before the throne, Vesper hears the crown-entity clearly — a chorus of dead kings — but beneath it, faintly, one living voice begging for help. She answers aloud. The court goes silent. Beat: first contact, and the terror of being heard.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Serane offers Vesper a bargain: help confirm whether the king is possessed, and Ilsa walks free. Serane's own sister was executed under the magic laws, and her loyalty to the Crown is a wound she dresses daily. Beat: reluctant alliance built on mutual damage.

chapters.title: Bone-Reading
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Examining a relic of the first Hollow King, Vesper learns the entity is an oath given flesh — a vow made by starving ancestors that outlived its purpose and now eats its hosts. The long winter falls when the host dies. Beat: the rules of the trap revealed.

chapters.title: Frost Letters
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric and Vesper establish a secret correspondence through frozen breath and carved tokens. He tells her about the boy he was before the coronation; she tells him about hearing his dead father apologize through a ring. Beat: intimacy growing in the narrow space surveillance allows.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A retired Warden recognizes Vesper's technique as her missing mother's, and reveals her mother didn't flee the city — she was taken to the palace years ago, to serve the crown. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance; Veper realizes she was always meant to be found.

chapters.title: Ilsa's True Page
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Freed per the bargain, Ilsa admits she forged her scholarship credentials and engineered their meeting: she's a member of the Unbound, a cell that wants the king dead, not saved, believing winter is a mercy. Beat: ally revealed as radical; the middle path narrows.

chapters.title: Court of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The entity grows stronger, puppeting Aldric publicly for hours at a time. A loyal chamberlain begins noticing the gaps and must choose between reporting the king or protecting him. Beat: the noose tightening; Aldric loses control of his own signature.

chapters.title: The Mother's Workshop
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Guided by the old Warden, Vesper finds her mother's hidden workshop beneath the palace chapel, full of half-carved bindings — including one unfinished piece labeled with Aldric's childhood name. Her mother tried this before and failed. Beat: hope and horror entwined; the family debt comes due.

chapters.title: Midwinter Court
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. At the midwinter feast, the entity forces Aldric to announce a purge of charm-sellers. Vesper, attending as Serane's 'consultant,' watches him condemn people like herself while his eyes plead. Beat: love tested publicly; Serane begins doubting which side the law serves.

chapters.title: What the Dead Want
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper communes with the chorus of dead kings inside the crown and learns the truth: they aren't tormentors but prisoners, each a host who failed, still bound by the original oath. They teach her the binding's grammar — and warn it requires a living hand willing to lose everything. Beat: enemies revealed as victims; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: The Unbound Move
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Unbound strike during the deep cold, seizing the palace vaults where the original oath-contract is kept, intending to burn it and kill the king mid-binding. Ilsa hesitates, having come to believe Vesper's way might work. Beat: civil fracture; Ilsa chooses sides at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Serane's Choice
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Ordered to execute Vesper as an Unbound collaborator, Serane instead arrests her own superior, burning her career in a single signature. She frees Vesper into the sealed palace with one instruction: 'Finish it before dawn, or we all freeze honestly.' Beat: loyalty realigned with truth over law.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The entity, wounded by the raid, abandons pretense and begins consuming Aldric outright to trigger the winter early. Snow rises past the windows. Aldric fights for his body from the inside, buying minutes with memories the entity cannot digest. Beat: darkest hour; the clock becomes literal.

chapters.title: Carving the King
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the throne room, Vesper performs the binding: carving the counter-oath into the crown-bone itself while the dead kings hold the entity's edges. It demands a price — the hand that binds surrenders what the dead gave her. She keeps carving as her hearing dies note by note. Beat: climax; sacrifice enacted in real time.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. From inside, Aldric feels the chorus release him one voice at a time, each dead king whispering thanks or warning. The entity, unmade from its oath, dissolves into ordinary snowfall. Aldric wakes truly in his own body for the first time in nine years — to find Vesper collapsed, silent, and breathing. Beat: release after long captivity.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Deaf to the dead for the first time in her life, Vesper convalesces in the palace, grieving her gift like a limb. Aldric sits with her without demanding conversation. She carves a small charm and, for once, hears nothing in it — and finds the silence isn't empty. Beat: mourning transformed into peace.

chapters.title: The Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Thaw comes early. Serane rebuilds the Wardens around protection rather than prohibition; Ilsa's survivors negotiate amnesty; the first charm-shop opens legally. Aldric, crowned but unbound, addresses a city learning to trust magic again. Beat: the world exhaling; institutions bending toward grace.

chapters.title: Odile and the Oath
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. A year later, Vesper teaches bone-carving apprentices who will never hear the dead — and that's the point. Aldric asks her, not the prophecy, what she wants next. She answers with a carved swan, odile, its wings open. Beat: love chosen freely, duty rewritten as promise kept together.
